# Configuration

Server configuration is entirely CLI flags; run `seavxrouter -h` for the full
list. No `.env` file is loaded automatically.

## Credentials file

`seavxrouter login` manages `~/.seavx/auth.jsonc`. JSON with `//` comments
allowed, mode `0600`. Never commit it or paste its contents into an issue.

```jsonc
// ~/.seavx/auth.jsonc — generated by `seavxrouter login`; keep private.
[
  {
    "provider": "antigravity",
    "access_token": "REDACTED",
    "refresh_token": "REDACTED",
    "expiry": "2026-11-14T10:03:42+07:00",
    "project_id": "REDACTED",
    "tier": "g1-pro-tier",
    "email": "you@example.com"
  },
  {
    "provider": "groq",
    "access_token": "gsk_REDACTED",
    "refresh_token": "",
    "expiry": "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  },
  {
    "provider": "cloudflare",
    "access_token": "REDACTED",
    "refresh_token": "",
    "expiry": "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "account_id": "REDACTED"
  },
  {
    "provider": "runcrate",
    "access_token": "rc_live_REDACTED",
    "refresh_token": "",
    "expiry": "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "base_url": "https://api.runcrate.ai/v1"
  }
]
```

Multiple entries for the same provider become accounts in that provider's
rotation pool. The running server watches this file; adding a provider or
account through `seavxrouter login` takes effect without a restart. Entries whose
credentials are unchanged keep their in-memory identity so per-account quota
state survives the reload.

Entries carrying `base_url` are custom OpenAI-compatible providers managed with
`seavxrouter provider add|list|remove`. The bearer `access_token` is sent to that
endpoint, and models use the `<provider>/<model>` prefix. Multiple keys for one
custom provider rotate, but they must all use the same base URL. Unlike `login`,
custom provider engines are built at startup: restart a running server after
adding or removing one.

## Environment variables

Optional variables that save typing during `seavxrouter login`; the OpenCode
ones also control how the running router reaches its local server:

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `NVIDIA_API_KEY` | Key read by `seavxrouter login nvidia` instead of prompting. |
| `GROQ_API_KEY` | Key read by `seavxrouter login groq` instead of prompting. |
| `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` | Token read by `seavxrouter login cloudflare`. |
| `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` | Account ID used by Cloudflare requests and login. |
| `OPENCODE_SERVER_URL` | Use an existing OpenCode v2 server instead of auto-starting one. |
| `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` | Basic-auth username for that server (default `opencode`). |
| `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` | Basic-auth password for that server. |
| `OPENCODE_BIN` | OpenCode binary to auto-start (default `opencode` on `PATH`). |

## Local state

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `~/.seavx/auth.jsonc` | Provider credentials, mode `0600`. |
| `~/.seavx/combos.jsonc` | Cross-provider model combos, mode `0600`. |
| `~/.seavx/usage.db` | SQLite usage ledger and recent request logs. |
| `~/.seavx/keys.db` | SQLite tenant API keys, monthly budgets, and token caps. |
| `~/.seavx/hidden-models.txt` | Optional model blocklist. |
| `~/.seavx/cache/models.json` | Cached models.dev pricing catalog. |
| `~/.seavx/server.url` | URL of the running server, used by the TUI. |
| `~/.config/systemd/user/seavxrouter.service` | Optional systemd user unit written by `seavxrouter service install`, mode `0600`. |

Set `-auth-file` to move `auth.jsonc`; `hidden-models.txt` and `combos.jsonc`
always sit next to it. Set `-usage-db` and `-keys-db` to relocate or disable
their databases (`off` disables). Keys stay usable with usage tracking off, but
budgets and token caps are not enforced in that case.

## Model combos

`combos.jsonc` defines ordered fallback lists requested as `combo/<name>`:

```jsonc
// ~/.seavx/combos.jsonc — managed by `seavxrouter combo`.
{
  "fast": ["groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b", "antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash"],
  "deep": ["codex/gpt-5", "antigravity/claude-sonnet-4-6"]
}
```

Members are full model IDs, tried left to right; bare IDs resolve like any
other request. A quota, auth, or transient failure before the first streamed
delta moves to the next member. A non-retryable error (for example a malformed
request) or a partially streamed answer ends the request, because the client
already saw output. Members pointing at unconfigured providers are skipped.
Nested `combo/` members are not allowed. Usage, cost, and request logs attribute
the member that actually answered; the response echoes `combo/<name>`. The file
is re-read on mtime change; another path can be set with `-combos`.

## Hidden models

`hidden-models.txt` removes model IDs from discovery and makes them
unrequestable (`404 model_not_found`). One entry per line:

```text
# literal IDs and provider-wide prefixes
nvidia/broken-model
codebuddy/
```

Blank lines and `#` comments are ignored. The file is re-read when its mtime
changes; no restart is needed.

## Usage and pricing

Every completed `/v1/*` request can be recorded in SQLite with token counts and
an estimated USD cost. Prices come from the models.dev catalog (cached locally)
with a built-in fallback. Override or extend with a JSON file:

```json
{
  "my-model": {"input": 0.5, "output": 1.5, "cached": 0.1}
}
```

```bash
./seavxrouter -pricing ./prices.json
```

Prices are USD per one million tokens. Disable tracking with `-usage-db off`.

## Request logs and compression

The newest 1,000 requests are retained with response bodies (up to 10 MB each),
status, latency, provider, model, serving account, user, and token usage. Request
bodies are read for routing hints but never persisted. The `account` field names
the credential that answered: the account email when known, else the upstream
account ID, else a short fingerprint of the API key. Read logs through
`/v1/logging` or the TUI; live entries arrive over `/v1/logging/stream`.

Large tool results in incoming requests are compressed before forwarding to
reduce prompt tokens. Tune with `-compress` and `-compress-min-bytes`; inspect
cumulative savings at `/v1/compression`.

## Quotas

Providers that expose quota report it at `/v1/quota`, aggregated per account.
Quota errors rotate accounts within the provider; a `combo/<name>` request is
the explicit way to fail over across providers, as described in
`references/providers.md`.

## Multi-tenant API keys (SaaS)

`-api-key` is the master/admin credential. Once it is set, customer keys minted
through `/v1/keys` or `seavxrouter key create` can call the inference endpoints
and `/v1/models`. Operator routes (`/v1/usage`, `/v1/logging*`, `/v1/quota`,
`/v1/compression`) and key management stay master-only.

- Keys are stored in `~/.seavx/keys.db`; only a SHA-256 hash is kept and the
  plaintext is shown once. Set `-keys-db off` to disable the feature.
- Usage and logs attribute a tenant request to `key:<name>`; filter with
  `GET /v1/usage?user=key:acme`.
- `budget_usd` is a monthly cap reset at 00:00 UTC on the 1st; `0` means
  unlimited. Exceeding it returns `429 insufficient_quota` on inference
  requests. Enforcement needs usage tracking; models without a price entry
  record cost 0 and do not consume budget.
- `limit_token` is a monthly cap on total tokens with the same reset; `0`
  means unlimited. Exceeding it also returns `429 insufficient_quota`. Priced
  and unpriced models both count their tokens.
- Revoking (`DELETE /v1/keys/{id}`) keeps the row and history; the key stops
  authenticating immediately.
- Running without `-api-key` leaves the server open and makes tenant keys inert.

## Security

- The server binds to `127.0.0.1` by default and has no authentication until
  `-api-key` is set. Never expose an unauthenticated instance to a network.
- Credentials are stored in plaintext (`0600`) so tokens can be refreshed.
  Protect the host and the file.
- `usage.db` contains response bodies and can contain sensitive data.
- For remote access, terminate TLS at a reverse proxy and require the API key.
- If a credential leaks, revoke it with the provider and log in again. Report
  vulnerabilities per `SECURITY.md`.
